result.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
result.summary: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop a theory for the organization of predictive information based on the scaling behavior of a family of information measures, and the theory predicts that if this organization has the same form at all measured length scales -- i.e., it has a self-similar structure -- then the information measures evaluated at different lengths collapse onto a common form. We observe this scaling collapse in long text documents, showing that predictive information is present at every length scale we measure and has a self-similar structure. Self-similarity is a considerably stronger property than showing the existence of long-range dependencies, and it constrains the process generating the text. More broadly, our results give quantitative support to the empirical observation that conditioning on more distant text continues to reveal new structure in language to LLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一套关于语言中预测信息组织的理论，基于一族信息度量的标度行为，并在长文档中观察到跨尺度的标度塌缩，说明预测信息在每个可测尺度上均存在且呈自相似结构。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息在不同历史长度上如何分布、何时饱和」的量化框架，可能为 LVR 中跨尺度视觉证据筛选、动态计算分配与长度泛化的预测提供问题表述和评价视角，但未涉及多模态或 latent 状态，需核查可迁移性。
